note: Merged/ready real issue fixing an error-handler message-loss bug in minimize-superseded-markers.mjs; today's A4 clear_verification criterion false-positives on its own error-handling description (known lexical-gate boundary gap).
title: fix(scripts): minimize-superseded-markers.mjs's runGh error handler loses e.message on empty stderr
body:
**Origin**: flagged by an adopter (`kurone-kito/dotfiles`) at `v0.6.0` (dotfiles#233), carried forward unfixed through `v0.7.0`/`v0.9.0`, reconfirmed still present verbatim at `v0.11.0` (`1f90787ebf4021673ce6e5eb69741df331fd2037`) by dotfiles#425's final-verification sweep.

**File**: `idd-template/scripts/minimize-superseded-markers.mjs`, `runGh`'s error handler.

**Problem**: The stderr fallback expression is:

```js
stderr: String(e.stderr?.toString?.() ?? e.message ?? 'unknown error'),
```

`??` only falls through on `null`/`undefined`. When `gh` exits with a defined-but-empty `stderr` string (e.g. on a bare timeout with no captured output), `e.stderr?.toString?.()` evaluates to `''` (empty string, not nullish), so the `??` chain short-circuits there and never reaches `e.message` -- discarding the actually-useful timeout/error text and reporting an empty string instead.

**Suggested fix**: Treat an empty string the same as nullish for this fallback, e.g.:

```js
stderr: (e.stderr?.toString?.() || e.message || 'unknown error'),
```

or an explicit empty-string check before falling through to `e.message`.

**Confirmed present** at `v0.11.0` verbatim (`idd-template/scripts/minimize-superseded-markers.mjs`, the `runGh` function).
